messages.subject: Initial Values in JAGS
parts:
Dear all,

I am currently having the same type of problem with initial values as described by Marc Kéry in the previous post.
I am working on a simple Occupancy model (that will be developed afterwards) that runs well with WinBUGS. 
I would like to test it with JAGS, but it seems that I have a problem with the initial values :
Error in jags.model(model.file, data = data, inits = init.values, n.chains = n.chains,  :

Error in node y[3,17]

Observed node inconsistent with unobserved parents at initialization.

Try setting appropriate initial values.

I tried with inits=NULL but I’m still having the same problem. If anyone has any suggestions on how I could set proper initial values in this case I would greatly appreciate it! I’m guessing it’s not very complicated but I’m a beginner in hierarchical models and I don’t see the solution here.

Please let me know if I should provide more information

Thank you!


Eva Delmas


MS student majoring in research in Ecology, Biodiversity and Evolution - Conservation Biology
University of Paris-Sud
eva.d...@u-psud.fr
&
Intern
UMR CNRS 7204 - Center for Ecology and Conservation Sciences - National Museum of Natural History

 ### LOAD DATA


 

year=”1996”

  detec_table<-list.files(pattern="detections")
  hours_table<-list.files(pattern="HRS")
  nhdays_table<-list.files(pattern="NHD")
  SiteCov_Table<-list.files(pattern="SITECOV")

  y<-read.table(detec_table, head=T, sep=",") #detection/non detection data
  ObsCov1<-read.table(hours_table, head=T, sep=",") #number of hours spent observing for each obs
  ObsCov2<-read.table(nhdays_table, head=T, sep=",") #number of half days spent observing for each obs
  SiteCov<-read.table(SiteCov_Table, head=T, sep=",") #Average annual Tmin at sites

  y<-as.matrix(y)
  nsites<-nrow(y)
  nsamples<-ncol(y)
  ObsCov1<-as.matrix(ObsCov1)
  ObsCov2<-as.matrix(ObsCov2)
  SiteCov<-SiteCov[,grep(paste("mean_",year,sep=""), names(SiteCov))]  

  #Standardize covariates

  meanObs1<-mean(ObsCov1, na.rm=T)
  sdObs1<-sd(ObsCov1[!is.na(ObsCov1)])
  OBSCOV1<-(ObsCov1-meanObs1)/sdObs1
  OBSCOV1[is.na(OBSCOV1)]<-0
  meanObs2<-mean(ObsCov2, na.rm=T)
  sdObs2<-sd(ObsCov2[!is.na(ObsCov2)])
  OBSCOV2<-(ObsCov2-meanObs2)/sdObs2
  OBSCOV2[is.na(OBSCOV2)]<-0
  meanSite<-mean(SiteCov, na.rm=T)
  sdSite<-sd(SiteCov[!is.na(SiteCov)])
  SITECOV<-(SiteCov-meanSite)/sdSite
  SITECOV[is.na(SITECOV)]<-0
  R=nsites
  T=nsamples



  library("R2WinBUGS")
  library("R2jags")  

  sink("modelSingleSingle.txt")
  cat("
      model{
     
      #PRIORS

      alpha.occ ~ dunif(-10,10)
      beta.occ ~ dunif(-10,10)
      beta2.occ ~ dunif(-10,10)
      alpha.p ~ dunif(-10,10)
      beta1.p ~ dunif(-10,10)
      beta2.p ~ dunif(-10,10)
      beta3.p ~ dunif(-10,10)
      beta4.p ~ dunif(-10,10)

     
      #LIKELIHOOD

      for (i in 1:R) {

      #True state model for the partially observed true state

      z[i] ~ dbern(psi[i])
      psi[i]<-1/(1+exp(-lpsi.lim[i]))
      lpsi.lim[i]<-min(999,max(-999,lpsi[i]))
      lpsi[i]<-alpha.occ+beta.occ*SITECOV[i]+beta2.occ*pow(SITECOV[i],2)

      for (j in 1:T) {

      #Observation model for the actual observations

      y[i,j] ~ dbern(mu.p[i,j])
      mu.p[i,j]<-z[i]*p[i,j]
      p[i,j]<-1/(1+exp(-lp.lim[i,j]))
      lp.lim[i,j]<-min(999,max(-999,lp[i,j]))
      lp[i,j]<-alpha.p+beta1.p*OBSCOV1[i,j]+beta2.p*pow(OBSCOV1[i,j],2)+beta3.p*OBSCOV2[i,j]+beta4.p*pow(OBSCOV2[i,j],2)

      } #j

      } #i

      occ.fs<-sum(z[])
      mean.p<-exp(alpha.p)/(1+exp(alpha.p))
      }
      ", fill=T)

sink()

jags.data<-list("y", "T", "R", "SITECOV", "OBSCOV1", "OBSCOV2")
win.data<-list(y=y, R=nsites, T=nsamples ,SITECOV=SITECOV,OBSCOV1=OBSCOV1,OBSCOV2=OBSCOV2)
z.init<-apply(y, 1, max, na.rm=TRUE)
inits<-function() {list(z=z.init, alpha.occ=runif(1,-1,-1), beta.occ=runif(1,-1,-1), beta2.occ=runif(1,-1,-1), alpha.p=runif(1,-1,-1), beta1.p=runif(1,-1,-1), beta2.p=runif(1,-1,-1), beta3.p=runif(1,-1,-1), beta4.p=runif(1,-1,-1))}
params<-c("alpha.occ", "beta.occ", "beta2.occ", "alpha.p", "beta1.p", "beta2.p", "beta3.p", "beta4.p", "occ.fs", "mean.p")

ni=10000 #number of iteration
nt=100  #n thin
nb=1000  #n burnin
nc=3  #n chains

 

#----------------------WinBUGS
#set WinBUGS directory
 bugs.dir<-"C:/Users/CESCO/Documents/WinBUGS14"
#run the model into WinBUGS
# out<-bugs(jags.data, inits, params, "modelSingleSingle.txt", n.chain=nc, n.thin=nt, n.iter=ni, n.burnin=nb, debug=TRUE, bugs.directory=bugs.dir,working.directory=getwd())

#----------------------JAGS
out<-jags(data=jags.data, inits=NULL, parameters.to.save=params, model.file="modelSingleSingle.txt", n.chains=nc, n.iter=ni, n.burnin=floor(ni/2), n.thin=max(1, floor((ni - nb) / 1000)), DIC=FALSE, working.directory=getwd(), refresh = ni/50, progress.bar = "gui", digits=4)

messages.author: 00ebeb6e0521112d
messages.subject: AW: Initial Values in JAGS
parts:
Salut Eva,

 

occupancy models are a classic example of the stubbornness of JAGS wrt inits.

 

Your model looks like this:

z_i ~Bernoulli(psi)                  # z is true presence-absence

y_ij ~Bernouli(z_i * p)          # presence/absence measurement error

 

The latent states (which are estimates of true presence/absence) are estimated as part of the MCMC algorithm. That is, they will get chains. You must initialize these chains such that any conflict between inits, model and data is avoided. A typical conflict is when you initialize the chain for z at 0 for a site where the species was detected at least once. In the classic model, which does not allow false positives, this is impossible and JAGS crashes.

 

So initialize your z either all at 1 or else at the observed state.

 

Kind regards  --- Marc

Hi Eva,

To add to what Marc advised, you might also try including only z in your initial value function (specified as Marc described above), allowing JAGS to choose its own values for alpha, beta, etc. That is typically the approach that works best for me so I don't accidentally force JAGS to use set of initial values for model parameters that conflict with the initial value of the latent state parameter.

Ken

Salut Eva,

 

occupancy models are a classic example of the stubbornness of JAGS wrt inits.

 

Your model looks like this:

z_i ~Bernoulli(psi)                  # z is true presence-absence

y_ij ~Bernouli(z_i * p)          # presence/absence measurement error

 

The latent states (which are estimates of true presence/absence) are estimated as part of the MCMC algorithm. That is, they will get chains. You must initialize these chains such that any conflict between inits, model and data is avoided. A typical conflict is when you initialize the chain for z at 0 for a site where the species was detected at least once. In the classic model, which does not allow false positives, this is impossible and JAGS crashes.

 

So initialize your z either all at 1 or else at the observed state.

 

Kind regards  --- Marc
